articles.title: In 1938, a Texas family bought a ranch near Austin; 87 years later, a 202-acre conservation deal added protection to a 6,600-acre landscape that holds 10% of the Barton Creek watershed
articles.summary: In 1938, Fred and Vera Shield of San Antonio bought a 5,300 acres on Barton Creek, beginning a multigenerational commitment to the land.
articles.body: In 1938, Fred and Vera Shield of San Antonio bought a 5,300 acres on Barton Creek, beginning a multigenerational commitment to the land. Roughly, nine decades later, that same family has added another layer of protection through a 202-acre conservation easement with the City of Austin. The agreement, announced in 2026, is part of a broader strategy to safeguard Shield Ranch, a 6,600-acre wildland that contains about 10 percent of the Barton Creek watershed and plays a vital role in the region’s water quality, according to The Nature Conservancy and Shield Ranch. A portion of the easement’s appraised value was purchased using funds from the city’s 2018 Water Quality Protection Lands Bond, with the balance donated by the Shield-Ayres-Bowen family, according to a report by Shield Ranch.A childhood shaped by wild landVera Ayres Bowen and her brother Bob Ayres grew up spending long summers at the ranch their grandparents, Fred and Vera Shield, bought in 1938. Every trip from San Antonio began with a shared meal with the couple who lived on the property and helped work the land. After that, the children were free to roam, picking peaches and pears from trees planted by their grandparents and hiking through clusters of Ashe juniper and oak.Bowen recalls discovering armadillos and snakes, riding a horse alone through the undeveloped landscape, and leaping off a boulder into the family swimming hole in Barton Creek. Those experiences, she says, gave her a sense of independence and confidence that stayed with her into adulthood. The joy and freedom she felt on the ranch ultimately inspired the family to protect the land for future generations through conservation easements, as per a report by The Nature Conservancy.Shield Ranch as the lungs of Barton CreekShield Ranch encompasses 6,600 acres of protected wildlands ringed by hills and teeming with wildlife. The property is designated a Quiet Place by Quiet Parks International and is home to endangered golden-cheeked warblers. Six miles of Barton Creek wind through the ranch, which is also listed as a historic district in the National Register.Jeff Francell, associate director of land protection for The Nature Conservancy in Texas, describes Shield Ranch as the lungs of Barton Creek. He notes that if the Ayres family had chosen a different path, the area could have become a large master-planned community with serious negative effects on water quality. The fact that it will remain relatively undeveloped forever helps preserve the clarity and health of Barton Creek, the report by The Nature Conservancy further shared.Layers of protection over decadesThe family’s conservation journey began in earnest after they developed their first ranch masterplan in the 1980s. They reached out to The Nature Conservancy in Texas to learn how they could protect the land, and the organisation served as a thought partner over the next decade. In the late 1990s, the Ayres family donated an easement on 4,670 acres to The Nature Conservancy, restricting certain types of development, as per Shield Ranch.They later sold an easement on an additional 1,676 acres to the City of Austin as part of its first voter-approved water protection program. The most recent 202-acre easement, announced in 2026, completes another chapter in this long-term strategy. A portion of the appraised value was purchased by the city using funds from the 2018 Water Quality Protection Lands Bond, while the balance was donated by the Shield-Ayres-Bowen family, as per the report.What the easements allow and prohibitThe conservation easements prohibit commercial development while allowing agricultural and recreational activities to continue. Limited development is permitted within strict parameters, including a small number of family residences and facilities for nonprofit organisations. This structure enables the family to maintain its stewardship role while ensuring the land’s ecological and hydrological functions remain intact.Under the terms of the agreements, officials from The Nature Conservancy and the City of Austin visit the property at least once a year to verify compliance. They also help troubleshoot any issues that arise on the ground. Bowen describes these agencies as great partners and says the family has benefited from their expertise and support over the years, as per reports.A camp that keeps the spirit aliveA 131-acre portion of the ranch is held by the nonprofit Shield Ranch Foundation, which operates Camp El Ranchito for youth who might not otherwise have access to outdoor programming. The camp moved into permanent, off-the-grid structures in 2022 and 2023, including a covered pavilion, rainwater collection tanks, evaporative toilets, and 11 sleeping shelters with walls that slide open to let in the breeze.The foundation works with organisations such as El Buen Samaritano and Westcave Outdoor Discovery Center to recruit students from fourth through twelfth grade. Bowen says her hope is that these campers will feel a kinship with the earth and become comfortable in nature, just as she and her siblings did as children. A stone monument on the site honours Indigenous people, European settlers, and ranchers who lived on the land before them, as per reports.Why this matters for Austin’s waterBarton Creek is a key contributor to Barton Springs, a beloved natural resource and drinking water source for the Austin area. As the city grows rapidly, pressure on surrounding land has increased. Shield Ranch sits in a zone where large-scale development could compromise water quality, hydrologic function, and biodiversity. The easements help ensure that this portion of the watershed remains a buffer against urban runoff and habitat loss.City leaders describe the ranch as part of a network of protected open space that represents a generational investment by Austin citizens. Voters have repeatedly approved taxpayer funds to permanently protect Barton Creek’s water quality, wildlife habitat, and open space. The 202-acre easement marks the completion of the 2018 bond program, which funded the permanent protection of more than 6,830 acres across the recharge and contributing zones for Barton Springs.A family legacy of stewardshipPatricia Shield Ayres, co-owner of Shield Ranch, says her family has been committed to land stewardship and natural resource conservation for nearly 90 years. The first conservation easement was donated in 1998, and each subsequent agreement reflects an ongoing commitment to safeguarding highly developable land along Barton Creek. Today, Shield Ranch Barton Creek is protected through three easements, one held by The Nature Conservancy and two by the City of Austin, as per Shield Ranch's website.Bowen frames the family’s role as one of temporary caretakers in a long line of stewards. She says their work was about caring for the land during their time and using tools like conservation easements to ensure it would remain wild for those who come after. Her hope is that 50 or 100 years from now, the ranch will look much as it does today, a rare and truly wild place in an increasingly urban region.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why 2 flydubai pilots were sitting among passengers when captain was stabbed
articles.summary: Four flydubai pilots were aboard Flight FZ1073 when the aircraft was thrown into chaos midair. But only two were in the cockpit.
articles.body: Four flydubai pilots were aboard Flight FZ1073 when the aircraft was thrown into chaos midair. But only two were in the cockpit.The other two were sitting among ordinary passengers until a violent attack on the flight deck turned them into the pilots who would help bring the Boeing 737 Max 8 safely down in Saudi Arabia.Reuters reported that the additional flydubai pilots took control after passengers intervened and gained access to the cockpit.The unusual situation raises a key question: why were four pilots on the same flight if only two were operating the aircraft?The New York Times reported that airlines generally do not place a second pair of pilots in the cockpit simply as a precaution. On a relatively short flight, carrying an additional operating crew would be expensive, as airlines have to pay highly trained and highly compensated pilots even when their services are not required for that particular flight.Instead, the other two pilots were travelling in the passenger cabin as part of a routine airline practice known as deadheading.Pilots routinely travel on flights they are not operating when an airline needs to position them at another location for a future assignment.flydubai confirmed that the crew members who helped secure and land the aircraft were “on-duty flydubai crew travelling on the flight.”During the incident, the co-pilot attacked and stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar, leaving the captain wounded and the aircraft plunging sharply.Reuters reported that the wounded captain, who was lying on the cockpit floor, managed to open the cockpit door during one of the dives, allowing passengers to rush in and overpower the co-pilot.It was at this point that the two additional flydubai pilots travelling in the cabin became crucial.After passengers gained access to the flight deck and subdued the co-pilot, the two off-duty flydubai pilots took control of the aircraft and safely landed it at Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia,You use AI every day. articles.title: Hull rapper Chiedu Oraka to perform at Music Matters Live in Singapore
articles.summary: Hull musician Chiedu Oraka is the only UK artist performing at Music Matters Live in Singapore.
articles.body:
Rapper Chiedu Oraka, who found fame supporting Coldplay during their Hull concert last year, says staying true to his core beliefs, seeded on a council estate, has taken him thousands of miles from home.

Later, he will be the only UK artist performing at Music Matters Live in Singapore.

Chiedu says he hopes to show the resilience, talent and ambition of his home city to an audience on the other side of the world.

"How is a rapper from North Hull rapping in Singapore? That doesn't even feel right and normal."

While on stage, Chiedu says he will be reflecting what life was like growing up on a council estate.

"The story is about determination, resilience, perseverance, not taking no for an answer," he tells BBC Radio Humberside .

Chiedu says he wants people from all over the world "to know that Hull is actually a good place and there's a lot of talent".

He adds: "I don't mind being the guy who flies the flag but just come and see us, come to The Deep. Come to all the nice restaurants, come to The Polar Bear, come to The Adelphi, we've got a lot here."

Chiedu went from doing shows in some of Hull's smaller clubs to performing in front of 25,000 people while supporting one of the world's biggest bands on tour.

In August last year, he supported Coldplay on the Hull leg of their Music of the Spheres world tour after receiving a personal call from frontman Chris Martin .

Chiedu says he is still on good terms with Martin and they still text each other.

"You might go on like a game show, someone asks you 'who's the most famous person in your phone book?' and I can say Chris Martin," he laughs.

Chiedu adds: "He's a proper top guy, he's just exactly what you see on the TV and on stage. He's just a proper, top bloke."

Despite his achievements, Chiedu remains humble and regularly pays homage to where he grew up through his music, even filming a music video on the estate where he used to live .

Another way he stays true to Hull is by never straying from his accent.

"It's the choice I made when I first started rapping," he says.

"When I first came onto the scene in Hull, there were Hull rappers rapping in a London accent. There were Hull rappers rapping in an American accent, which is crazy to me."

He adds: "I just wanted to be true to myself....Hull is such an honest place.

"Hull wouldn't even let me get away with rapping in anything else than a broad North Hull Estate accent."

Chiedu also highlights the recent successes of Hull City and says he will be wearing the club's colours on stage.

"I get so much love from the people of Hull," he says. "People are always so complimentary. People always want photos. People always want to speak to me.

"I'm so lucky because I know there's a lot of artists that don't get that love from their city. I'm very blessed that I do."

Chiedu praises the PRS Foundation and the International Showcase Fund for helping him with the funds to get to Singapore and play at the festival.

"If it wasn't for them, I wouldn't be going," he says.

"I'm just so blessed that I even get to do these things. It's mad that this is my job."

articles.title: Migration Museum given less space at 65 Crutched Friars
articles.summary: The museum was originally to be given three floors of a 21-storey tower block in the City of London.
articles.body:
London's Migration Museum will be given a third less space than originally agreed in a new 21-storey block, to allow for more student accommodation.

The museum, which explores how movement to and from the UK shapes the nation, was offered a permanent rent-free home for 60 years at 65 Crutched Friars in the City of London under a scheme by developer Dominus.

In plans approved in 2023, the museum was given three floors. But on Wednesday, City of London Corporation members signed off on revised plans for two floors for the museum.

Laurie Boult, chief executive of the museum, said the decision gave them "certainty" that it could proceed with the project.

During the meeting, some corporation members raised concerns about the revised plans.

The Migration Museum has moved between a series of temporary sites since it was founded in 2011.

The revised scheme at 65 Crutched Friars reduces the museum's space by one floor in favour of an additional 33 student rooms on level two, bringing the total number to 815.

Corporation officers had recommended the changes be approved, and said that the museum space would "remain a significant and publicly accessible cultural use".

Jay Ahluwalia, principal director at Dominus, said they had worked with the Migration Museum on the revised proposals.

Charles Gurassa, chair of the Board of Trustees at the Migration Museum, said that even with the reduction, the new site would offer about 40% more space than the museum's previous temporary home.

The application was approved by members, with all but two of the 15 present voting in favour.

articles.title: John Denver’s former Aspen guesthouse and music studio sold for $4.75 million in 2023; later the new owner sold the 2,912-sq-ft five-bedroom home for $8.2 million in 2025
articles.summary: John Denver’s former guest house and music studio in Aspen, Colorado, has proved to be a valuable piece of real estate.
articles.body: John Denver’s former guest house and music studio in Aspen, Colorado, has proved to be a valuable piece of real estate. The home, which sits on a 5-acre lot in Starwood, was once part of the singer’s estate, where he lived from the early 1970s until his death in a plane crash in 1997. The Aspen home was never his main residence, so the absence of a functional kitchen is understandable. The previous owners sold it ‘as is’ with some ‘deferred maintenance’, listing agent P.J. Bory of Christie’s International Real Estate Aspen Snowmass told Mansion Global.In April 2023, a Florida-based physician bought it for $4.75 million, then repaired the roof, replaced the sliding glass doors that face the mountains, and added a modern kitchen, a hot tub and a new deck. A year later, in June 2024, the property was listed for $8.495 million, but ended without a sale. Then, after a year, it was relisted at $8.595 million and closed in November 2025 at $8.2 million.A fixer-upper with a famous pastIn 2016, the main house was sold, and the remaining guest house and music studio became a separate 5-acre property. The larger structure had three bedrooms. The guest house and garage, once Denver’s studio, had two. In his 1971 song ‘Starwood in Aspen’, Denver described the neighbourhood, and the address, of course, carried the weight of his name. Starwood is one of the only gated communities in Aspen, and Denver funded its 24/7 security in the beginning, according to Bory. The property came with private tennis courts, cross-country ski trails, horse pastures and a fire station of its own.Its previous owners had sold the place ‘as is’ with some deferred maintenance when the house was first listed. By the time the house reached the market in 2024, the roof had been repaired. The sliding glass doors that line the front and face the mountains had all been replaced. In April 2024, the Florida-based physician bought it through a trust for $4.75 million. There was no functional kitchen, so he added a modern one that flows into the open dining and living areas.“He’s a fan, and he thought it would be a fun project to do,” Bory recalled. With the renovation, the seller also added a hot tub, a new deck and overhauled the property’s landscaping, which had been let go and overtaken by scrub oak, the agent added.The work was mostly structural rather than aesthetic, so a good deal of Denver’s era survived. Tile in some of the bathrooms. The wood beams. A stained-glass partition that came from the original main house.“That was always his intention, to embrace the vibe of John Denver and what his original design was,” Bory told the outlet.What the buyer getsThe buyer got more house than the square footage suggests. The 2,912 square feet are split across two structures, a three-bedroom main building and a two-bedroom guest house that doubled as Denver’s studio. This sits on 5 acres inside gated Starwood, where the amenities include 24/7 security, private tennis courts, cross-country ski trails, horse pastures and a fire station of its own.There are 2,912 square feet of living space in total, so the next owner has the opportunity to build on top of the existing house and also expand it to the allowed 5,750 square feet without having to buy more development rights, according to the agent.Besides its famous history, the property’s biggest highlight is the view that runs from Aspen to Snowmass, including the area’s four ski mountains.“It’s about 10 to 12 minutes from downtown Aspen, and you’re sitting on 5 acres with the best views of Aspen and our valley that you could possibly imagine, so you kind of have the best of both worlds,” Bory said.No wonder the sale closed in November 2025 at $8.2 million.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: Vilnius airport in Lithuania was temporarily closed and Nato air-policing fighter jets were scrambled after a possible drone was detected flying from the direction of Belarus, Lithuania's National Crisis Control Centre told news agency Reuters.Authorities advised residents in the Vilnius region to be prepared to seek shelter if necessary, it said.The incident comes as security concerns continue to rise across the Baltic region, where countries bordering or located near Russia and Belarus have reported a growing number of airspace incidents linked to the war in Ukraine.Lithuania is a Nato and European Union (EU) member and has been closely monitoring developments along its borders amid concerns about possible Russian aggression. Russia has rejected allegations that it is planning an attack on Nato, while Western officials have said Moscow does not currently have the capability for a direct assault.The development unflods as neighbouring Latvia prepares for a parliamentary election on Saturday, with security concerns featuring prominently in the campaign.Opinion polls have placed Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List at around 14%, narrowly ahead of the overtly pro-Russian Sovereign Power. However, political fragmentation could make it difficult to form a government after the election.Kulbergs, a 47-year-old businessman and amateur rally driver, took office in May after the previous coalition collapsed over its handling of incidents involving military drones that entered Latvian airspace without being detected.The drones were Ukrainian, although Latvian officials blamed Russia for causing them to stray from their intended flight paths.The incident in Lithuania is likely to add to security concerns across the Baltics, where governments have remained on alert over airspace violations and the wider regional impact of the Russia-Ukraine war.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Could no longer defend the indefensible': Former AAP spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joins Congress
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Aam Aadmi Party(AAP) spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday, saying she could no longer defend the “indefensible”.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Aam Aadmi Party(AAP) spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday, saying she could no longer defend the “indefensible”.Explaining her decision to leave AAP, Kakkar said, “There was a time when it was said that AAP would not take a bungalow or a car. But later, choppers started being used for private travel, and I could no longer defend the indefensible.”“I drew a line when I saw that the Aam Aadmi Party, which at one point had attracted people with great substance and intelligence, was unable to retain them,” she added.She also questioned the appointment of people to senior positions in Punjab. “Who are the people being brought in now? New people who have not even worked at the booth level are being brought from Rajasthan and given senior positions in Punjab, along with bungalows and cars,” Kakkar said.“How long can I defend the indefensible?” she added.Kakkar also praised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, calling him resilient and saying she had seen him and the party withstand attacks.“If there is one leader who is not afraid to promote his ideas, it is Rahul Gandhi. I observed that he is the only leader who has not shed tears for the cameras. He is the only leader today who has not done that. He is resilient. I have seen how he was humiliated and how an entire machinery was deployed to put him down. But Rahul Gandhi and the Congress remained resilient,” she said.“Their authenticity is their soul. I saw that there is a soul in this party as well, which I found missing in other parties. And I say this from lived experience,” she added.Kakkar also backed Rahul Gandhi's criticism of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over electoral-roll revision and his allegations concerning voters' rights.“I also saw how Rahul Gandhi has continuously launched a campaign against traitor Gyanesh Kumar. He has made everyone, including us, aware of this issue,” Kakkar said.“We have to make the public aware of how, according to him, our only voting right is being stolen by Gyanesh Kumar and put into PM Modi's account. This has to stop. Therefore, we must all come together now to support the Congress and support Rahul Gandhi in his authentic fight to keep the idea of India alive,” she added.Kakkar later called for opposition unity and urged people to join the Congress.“Now, we all have to come under one umbrella so that no votes are divided or scattered, because, as 'traitor' Gyanesh Kumar is already stealing votes and putting them into PM Modi's account. We must not give them any more opportunities. Everyone must come under one umbrella, under the Congress, to defeat PM Modi and his regressive politics,” she said.The Congress also said in a post on X that three prominent figures had joined the party, including, Priyanka Kakkar, former Uttar Pradesh MLA Shyam Sundar Sharma and journalist Rajat Rakesh Tandon.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia escalates Ukraine infrastructure attacks, strikes second Kyiv bridge in days
articles.summary: Russia struck a second major bridge in Kyiv within days on Saturday, damaging the road surface and trolleybus cables and forcing the suspension of traffic
articles.body: Russia struck a second major bridge in Kyiv within days on Saturday, damaging the road surface and trolleybus cables and forcing the suspension of traffic across the Dnipro, as Moscow stepped up attacks on critical infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital.The Northern Bridge was hit during a Russian air attack, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Emergency services were deployed to the scene, while traffic from the east bank to the west bank was blocked. No casualties were reported.The strike came after Russia repeatedly targeted Kyiv’s Southern Bridge with drones on Thursday and Friday, disrupting one of the capital’s key transport links.The attacks on the two bridges mark a new phase in the latest Russian campaign against Kyiv’s infrastructure. The bridges connect the eastern and western sides of the city, whose roughly 3 million residents depend heavily on the transport network to cross the Dnipro.Kyiv’s bridges come under repeated attackThe Southern Bridge was struck several times over the previous two days, forcing authorities to temporarily suspend traffic across it as well as two other bridges over the Dnipro.The attacks caused major disruption for commuters. More than a third of Kyiv’s residents lived on the eastern, or “left”, bank of the river before Russia’s 2022 invasion, while most government institutions and companies are located on the western, or “right”, bank.Klitschko had earlier warned that the attacks were putting Kyiv in a “very dramatic situation” as Russian strikes hit the city’s critical infrastructure, logistics and housing.After one strike on the Southern Bridge, passengers described how the blast wave sent dust through the ventilation system of a train carriage.The latest attacks have revived memories of last winter, when Russia launched some of the war’s most damaging strikes against infrastructure supplying Kyiv with power.The attacks came after Russia launched what Ukraine viewed as the opening salvo of an expected winter campaign targeting energy facilities serving the capital.Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia was seeking to destroy not only bridges but also data centres, internet and mobile networks, hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure in an effort to force people to leave Ukrainian cities.Russia has previously denied systematically targeting civilians during its bombing campaigns.Russian president Vladimir Putin has said Moscow’s attacks are a response to Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. articles.title: Xi Jinping unwell? Chinese officials sought unusual long breaks during the US visit
articles.summary: Fresh questions have emerged over Chinese President Xi Jinping's health after unusual arrangements made for him to rest during his recent summit with US
articles.body: Fresh questions have emerged over Chinese President Xi Jinping's health after unusual arrangements made for him to rest during his recent summit with US President Donald Trump, reported by Wall Street Journal.People familiar with the planning told WSJ, Chinese officials asked the White House for a private room where Xi could rest between engagements and sought more downtime during his Washington visit.Hold roomThe most unusual detail was the request for a private “hold room” inside the White House's West Wing. According to the WSJ, Xi's wife Peng Liyuan was reportedly the only other person allowed inside the room, while even Cai Qi, a senior member of Xi's delegation and his chief of staff, was not permitted to use it.The arrangement was described by a former US National Security Council official as unusual compared with previous visits by foreign leaders.Chinese officials also turned down a planned working lunch between Xi and Trump on September 24, the only full day of his Washington visit, saying they wanted more time for Xi to rest. The decision created a roughly five-hour gap in the summit schedule.Holding handsAt Joint Base Andrews, footage reviewed by the WSJ showed Xi holding Peng's hand while using the aircraft's railing as he descended the stairs.Two days later, while climbing the National Archives steps alongside Trump and Melania Trump, Xi again held Peng's hand, with the WSJ reporting that he appeared to rely on her for support.The unusual scheduling was also visible elsewhere in Xi's itinerary. No official engagements were planned for him on the evening of his arrival following a roughly 14-hour flight from Beijing, while his visit to the US National Archives the following day lasted only about 10 minutes, far shorter than initially planned, according to the WSJ.BRICS summitThe latest report has also brought renewed attention to Xi's health during his recent visit to India for the BRICS summit.During the opening session in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly appeared to check on Xi, asking his interpreter, “Is it okay?” after the Chinese president appeared uncomfortable.Xi later skipped a gala dinner hosted by Modi for BRICS leaders and other dignitaries after attending the first day of the summit and holding a bilateral meeting with Modi.Taken together, the episodes have renewed questions over Xi's health, though no specific illness has been established. articles.title: Eight rope bridges over an Amazon road recorded 15,000 wildlife crossings in Brazil; not a single roadkill was recorded
articles.summary: In Alta Floresta, a small Amazon town in northern Mato Grosso, eight rope bridges installed in 2024 now span the road leading into town, and the results
articles.body: In Alta Floresta, a small Amazon town in northern Mato Grosso, eight rope bridges installed in 2024 now span the road leading into town, and the results after 15 months are striking. Camera traps recorded about 15,000 safe crossings by tree-dwelling animals, including several monkey species, and not a single roadkill. The bridges come from Projeto Reconecta, founded by biologist Fernanda Abra, and are now being expanded in other parts of Brazil and in Suriname. Brazil's National Department of Transport Infrastructure has also named the design its recommended highway standard, which could bring similar crossings to roads across the country.Why roads are deadly for Brazilian wildlife and the domino effect on Amazon forestsBrazil has the greatest diversity of primates in the world and also the fourth-largest road network, a dangerous combination for animals living along forest edges split apart by highways. A 2022 study ‘How Many Mammals Are Killed on Brazilian Roads? Assessing Impacts and Conservation Implications’ found that nearly 9 million mammals are killed on Brazil's roads every year.The harm goes beyond collisions. Animals that come down from the trees to cross a road can be hit by vehicles, while strictly tree-dwelling species avoid the ground altogether and end up isolated by the road as a barrier. Isolated populations grow smaller and more vulnerable, and without gene flow between groups, a species loses genetic diversity.As per Mongabay, primatologist Fabiano Rodrigues de Melo describes a domino effect, losing fruit-eating primates can change the makeup of a forest, because they help disperse seeds and even contribute to pollination.Which monkeys and other animals use the aerial crossingsAbra wanted a solution that was simple, low in cost and durable. The current bridge has a multilayer design that suits animals that move in different ways, including species that rely on prehensile tails, arm-swinging species such as spider monkeys, and species that simply walk across a network of crossed ropes.Every bridge carries two camera traps, one facing the crossing to record which animals use it, and one facing the forest to see which animals arrive but decide not to cross. Primates recorded in the first months included the black-faced black spider monkey, the Purus red howler monkey, the northern night monkey, the tufted capuchin, Schneider's marmoset and the Alta Floresta titi monkey. Opossums, sloths and mouse opossums have also been seen using the bridges.The titi monkey has special meaning for the project. It was described only in 2019, was soon classified as critically endangered, and has become the symbol of the initiative.15,000 camera trap crossings, zero roadkill and the slow pace of animal adaptationThe eight bridges were installed in 2024, and over 15 months the camera trap footage showed 15,000 safe crossings by tree-dwelling animals and no roadkill. The project involves the municipal government along with local organisations and business owners.The animals did not all adapt at the same speed. Tufted capuchins took seven months before using one of the bridges for the first time, which may suggest that each species has its own pace. Abra says this is why patience matters. She notes that conservation urgency often ignores the time an impact takes to unfold.Lessons from Highway 174 and the Waimiri-Atroari Indigenous territory, where Reconecta beganAlta Floresta is not the project's first site. In 2021, working with the Waimiri-Atroari Indigenous people, the team installed 32 canopy bridges over Highway 174, which crosses their territory and the Amazon between the states of Amazonas and Roraima. The project's own website gives a figure of 30 bridges on that road, so the count appears to have changed over time. The website credits the Smithsonian Institution, the Waimiri-Atroari people, the Federal University of Amazonas and the National Department of Transport Infrastructure as partners, and describes combining modern technology with traditional Indigenous knowledge.Over five years, cameras on the bridge poles have documented about 1,250 primate crossings there, including the golden-handed tamarin, which often descends to the ground and is therefore especially vulnerable to roadkill. That highway was built in the 1970s, and monitoring shows that animals use the structures more as time passes.National standards for wildlife crossings and expansion to other locationsAbra said eight more bridges would be installed in Alta Floresta's urban area in August, after the electric utility lowers and insulates power lines so animals jumping from a bridge onto the wires are not electrocuted. New chapters are planned in Suriname and in Lucas do Rio Verde, which will install 10 canopy bridges.The wider policy picture is also shifting. In 2026, Brazil's National Department of Transport Infrastructure designated the rope bridge design as the recommended standard for highways. A bill to create a National Road Safety Plan for Wildlife has passed the Chamber of Deputies and awaits a vote in the Senate.Abra also hopes to reach other habitats. She points to the highway through the Pantanal known as the "highway of death," where roughly 2,000 animals are killed each year, and to the Atlantic Forest, home to threatened monkeys such as muriquis and howler monkeys.You use AI every day. articles.title: homemade bombs part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told
articles.summary: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur, considered the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
articles.body:
Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb.

Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.

One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025.

Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat in 2020, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London.

As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford.

The Metropolitan Police said the men were alleged to have obtained instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquired liquids and other components to make an improvised explosive device and researched and carried out reconnaissance on potential targets.

The prosecution say they carried out "hostile reconnaissance" on buildings in Manchester including the Heaton Park synagogue - where two British Jews, Melvin Kravitz and Adrian Daulby, were killed when it was attacked during last year's Yom Kippur service - and also at the city's Jewish Museum.

The court heard the defendants are alleged to have been directed by another Iranian individual who is believed to be in Iran.

The men, wearing grey tracksuits, stood in the dock of court five and spoke through translators only to confirm their name, date of birth and addresses.

She said "the fact both suspects arrived by small boat several years ago" was a reminder of the "importance of work to tackle illegal migration".

"We will be unrelenting in our efforts to protect our Jewish communities, root out antisemitism in this country, and maintain our border security," she added.

articles.title: 'Recovering well': MEA provides update on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar attacked by co-pilot
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Saturday said flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar was recovering well after he was attacked by his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Saturday said flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar was recovering well after he was attacked by his co-pilot during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.The MEA said Machchhar remained under “excellent medical care” and that it was in touch with his family and local authorities.“Indian braveheart Capt. Smit remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well. We are in touch with his family & local authorities, extending support for a speedy recovery. Our thanks to UAE gov. for their care. We join well-wishers in praying for his good health,” Indian embassy in UAE said in a post on X.The attack took place on September 30 aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Tel Aviv. According to the UAE's state news agency WAM, citing attorney general counsellor Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, the Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, attacked Machchhar with a cockpit crash axe while attempting to take control of the aircraft.Co-pilot allegedly tried to seize controlThe UAE attorney general said al-Hammami “attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and sought to seize command of the aircraft's piloting instruments while the plane was airborne.The assault triggered a violent struggle inside the cockpit, during which the aircraft reportedly lost about 16,000 feet in two minutes, according to reports on the incident. Machchhar, despite sustaining serious injuries, fought back and managed to unlock the cockpit door.Crew members, passengers and two off-duty pilots then entered the cockpit and helped overpower the co-pilot, allowing the aircraft to be stabilised.The flight subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 180 people on board safely disembarked.A crash axe is a standard emergency tool kept in aircraft cockpits and is designed to help pilots cut through aircraft materials during emergencies.UAE investigation underwayThe UAE authorities are investigating the incident to establish the circumstances, motive and possible connections linked to the attack.“The conclusive findings will be made public immediately once all mandatory legal and administrative steps have successfully concluded,” al-Shamsi said, according to WAM.Investigators are also examining physical and digital evidence as part of the probe.Reports raise questions over co-pilot's backgroundMedia reports have also raised questions about al-Hammami's background and previous aviation career.According to sources cited by CBS News and Al Arabiya English, al-Hammami had previously undergone pilot training with Oman Air. He was reportedly moved to desk duties after authorities detected visits to radical websites and later resigned around 2024. Reports also said he had previously been barred from flying in Oman over extremist concerns linked to an earlier stay in Syria.After moving to Dubai, he was hired by flydubai, with reports raising questions about whether the Omani government was formally involved in his background checks.CNN also reported that posts appeared on a LinkedIn profile associated with al-Hammami after the incident, including cockpit footage of an El Al aircraft and images of Al-Qaeda figures. The authenticity and circumstances surrounding those posts remain part of the broader scrutiny of the case.The UAE authorities have not yet released their final findings on the motive behind the attack or the circumstances that led to al-Hammami's actions. The investigation remains ongoing.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IAF chief hints at 'foreign options' for 5th-gen jets, flags Pakistan-China tie-up
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Air Force Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh on Saturday said that Pakistan's collaboration with China to build fifth-generation fighter
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Air Force Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh on Saturday said that Pakistan's collaboration with China to build fifth-generation fighter jets is a "cause for concern" for India.At the annual press conference, Singh said that the IAF will be able to ward off the threat for the time being, but India must induct fifth-generation fighter jets quickly."It is a cause for worry, no doubt. But is it a situation which is a total no-go situation? I would not agree to that. We do have capabilities. It is not that one platform matters so much. It is the integration of that platform into your system. Just as Pakistan had other platforms, when we carried out Operation Sindoor, they could not do much with them," Singh said."So, as we purchase various platforms and induct them, we must ensure that they are properly integrated into our system. So, we should be able to ward off this threat for the time being, till they integrate it into their system very well. For the future, we need to think ahead. We need to bring in a fifth-generation aircraft quickly. We have to push the AMCA programme. And if there are delays in it, we need to take some other decisions," he added.During the presser, Singh said that the IAF currently has 29 fighter squadrons against an authorised strength of 42. He said that the force needs to induct 36 to 40 fighter aircraft every year to address the shortfall.“We may have to look at other fighter platforms in case of delays in AMCA fifth-gen, other programmes,” he said.On the possibility of an alternative fifth-generation fighter, Singh said Russia has offered its Su-57 jets to India, but no decision has been taken on the proposal.Russia has publicly pitched the Su-57 to India, with Russian President Vladimir Putin also offering joint production of the aircraft in India. However, Singh's remarks indicate that the IAF has not taken a decision on the Russian offer.Last week, defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh had said that India had not decided to pursue any foreign fifth-generation fighter programme and remained committed to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) as its indigenous fifth-generation fighter project.The AMCA programme, however, has been under timeline pressure. The Aeronautical Development Agency recently extended the deadline for industry proposals to October 30, with bids scheduled to be opened on October 31.The IAF currently does not operate a fifth-generation stealth fighter, either indigenous or foreign. The first AMCA prototype is expected to take to the skies in 2028, with induction planned in the years that follow.The programme is aimed at giving India a domestically designed and manufactured stealth combat aircraft and reducing its dependence on foreign platforms for this capability.

articles.title: A Texas family has owned a 650-acre Lake Palestine ranch since 1940 and used it for its pecan business; 86 years later, a $10 million deal will turn the property into a new state park
articles.summary: A 650-acre ranch on the shores of Lake Palestine in East Texas, owned by the same family since 1940 and long associated with a pecan-growing business, is
articles.body: A 650-acre ranch on the shores of Lake Palestine in East Texas, owned by the same family since 1940 and long associated with a pecan-growing business, is set to become Texas' next state park after the property was acquired for more than $10 million. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation closed the purchase on October 1, 2026, securing one of the largest remaining contiguous tracts of land along the lake, reported The Texas Tribune and The Dallas Morning News.The property, in Henderson County between Tyler and Athens, will not immediately open as a public park. The foundation plans to hold the land until the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) can acquire it, likely in late 2027, using additional funding from the voter-approved Centennial Parks Conservation Fund. Development will then take place in phases, meaning visitors may have to wait several years before the full park is operational.History stretching back more than eight decadesThe Pollard family has owned the property since 1940, when it became part of the family's Texas Pecan Nursery operation. The ranch was used to grow pecans and later to sell pecan trees, while portions of the property remained relatively undeveloped. For the Pollard family, it was also a place for hunting, fishing and spending time together across generations.Now, the family property is headed for a very different future. Sam Pollard, president of Texas Pecan Nursery, described the land as deeply personal to his family. “This land is part of my soul,” Pollard said, adding that it meant a great deal to him that the property could become a legacy for others to enjoy.The proposed park occupies a strategically important stretch of Lake Palestine. The property has about 2,000 feet of lake frontage and is located roughly 18 miles west of Tyler and 20 miles east of Athens. It contains native East Texas pine forests, grassland, a pecan orchard, ponds and other water features.The site also contains a 58-foot-deep lake and approximately 10 ponds, according to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation. The property provides habitat for white-tailed deer, bobcats, waterfowl and other birds and wildlife, giving the proposed park both recreational and conservation value.Lake Palestine itself is a major recreational reservoir in East Texas. The Texas Water Development Board says the lake was created by the Blackburn Crossing Dam on the Neches River. Construction of the original dam began in 1960 and was completed in 1962, while a later enlargement was completed in 1971. The reservoir covers more than 23,000 acres at conservation-pool level, according to the agency's data.The new park would add a significant publicly accessible tract to that landscape. According to TPWD and the foundation, potential future activities include hiking, biking, boating, paddling, swimming and fishing, along with day-use areas, camping and lakefront recreation. Planned amenities include hike-and-bike trails, traditional and primitive campsites and areas for visitors to spend time along the lake.Development to take place in phasesBut officials have stressed that the property will not suddenly become a fully developed state park after the purchase.TPWD plans to open the future park in phases, beginning with guided access before expanding to day-use facilities and eventually overnight access. The agency also intends to carry out habitat restoration and seek public input on the property's future after it formally acquires the land.The unusual arrangement behind the purchase is part of the story. Rather than waiting for the state to complete its acquisition, the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, a nonprofit organisation that supports the state's parks and wildlife programmes, stepped in and bought the property first. It will temporarily hold the land while TPWD waits for additional money from the Centennial Parks Conservation Fund, allowing the state to preserve the opportunity to acquire the property rather than risk losing it to another buyer.The Centennial Parks Conservation Fund was established after Texas lawmakers approved a $1 billion investment in 2023 for the purchase and development of state parks. The Lake Palestine property is among the projects being advanced through this broader expansion of Texas' public-land system.Anne Brown, executive director of the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, said opportunities to protect properties of this scale and location are uncommon and that timing was important in securing the ranch. She described the acquisition as an example of how a public-private partnership can help conserve land for future generations.Rodney Franklin, director of Texas State Parks, also highlighted the property's combination of lake access and its existing pecan trees. “We are excited to add this East Texas gem to the Texas State Park system,” Franklin said, noting that families would eventually be able to enjoy Lake Palestine along with the pecan trees that are a signature feature of the property.The property's potential was apparently visible even before the purchase was completed. Josh Smith, a co-founder of TexasLand, the brokerage that represented the Pollard family, recalled his first visit to the ranch and said, “This place looks like a state park.” He said TPWD officials subsequently carried out extensive site visits and evaluations involving agency leaders, park planners and wildlife biologists.The property remained under contract for nearly a year while those studies were completed. The foundation ultimately closed the deal for more than $10 million, according to its October 2 announcement. The NextEra Energy Foundation contributed $100,000 to the project, while the foundation also used its donor-supported Land Conservation Loan Fund to help move quickly on the acquisition.You use AI every day. articles.title: North Korea test fires ballistic missile after Seoul demands apology for landmine blast
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's sister Kim Yo Jong said on Saturday that an intermediate-range strategic missile had been tested earlier in the morning,
articles.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's sister Kim Yo Jong said on Saturday that an intermediate-range strategic missile had been tested earlier in the morning, hours after South Korea reported a ballistic missile launch towards the sea.“North Korea's Kim Yo Jong says an intermediate-range strategic missile was used for the drill,” state news agency KCNA reported.Kim Yo Jong, a director of North Korea’s ruling party, said an intermediate-range missile was used in a drill involving a “strategic weapon” towards the sea off the country’s east coast. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the drill, carried out by “a firepower sub-unit undertaking an exclusive special mission”, she said, according to Reuters.Citing South Korean and Japanese assessments of the missile’s flight distance, Jong said they showed limitations in tracking capabilities. “Whenever we applied the wave-like trajectory mode to missiles, the enemy failed to track the targets from their first skip points,” she said, adding that the weapon could alter its flight orbit at low altitude using artificial intelligence technology.“In other words, this means that there is no way to avoid this attack,” she said.Earlier, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff had said the missile was launched from the Wonsan area on the country's eastern coast and flew more than 700 km (435 miles) towards the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan. South Korean and US militaries were analysing the specifics of the launch.Japan's defence ministry said the missile landed outside the country's exclusive economic zone.The South Korean military said it had strengthened surveillance and vigilance for possible further launches and was closely sharing information with the US and Japan.Seoul's presidential national security office called on Pyongyang to halt its repeated ballistic missile launches, describing them as a violation of UN Security Council sanctions and “a serious act that does nothing to help manage the current situation”.The US Pacific Command said the launch “does not pose an immediate threat to U.S. personnel or territory, or to our allies.”The launch came a day after Kim Yo Jong dismissed South Korean demands for an apology over a September 21 landmine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers near the military demarcation line.South Korea and the US-led UN Command said a joint inspection found that the blast was caused by mines planted by North Korea. The command later said North Korea had violated the armistice agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.Kim Yo Jong rejected Seoul's demands as “utterly pathetic” and said North Korea intended to cut ties with South Korea permanently. In a separate KCNA report, she called Seoul “despicable” and described a proposal by South Korean unification minister Chung Dong-young for border talks as a “wild dream and unilateral jargon”.The latest launch follows a series of North Korean military activities in recent weeks, including missile tests, live-fire exercises and the commissioning of a new warship. Wonsan was also the site of a September 20 test that North Korean state media described as involving a hypersonic missile system.South Korean president Lee Jae Myung has urged Pyongyang to return to dialogue, while US President Donald Trump's recent outreach has raised concerns in Seoul about its role in any future nuclear negotiations.North Korea has so far rejected Trump's overtures, saying Washington must first abandon what Pyongyang calls its “hostile policy” and drop denuclearisation as a precondition for talks.

articles.title: After 40 years as one of the Great Lakes' most degraded sites, Muskegon Lake had 347,350 tons of debris and 190,000 tons of contaminated soil removed
articles.summary: Muskegon Lake in Michigan has been removed from the US Environmental Protection Agency’s Areas of Concern list after about decades of restoration work.
articles.body: Muskegon Lake in Michigan has been removed from the US Environmental Protection Agency’s Areas of Concern list after about decades of restoration work. The lake was designated one of the most environmentally degraded sites in the Great Lakes about 40 years ago. In September 2025, it was officially removed from the list after restoration efforts addressed problems including habitat loss, contaminated soils, and hardened shorelines.Since 2008, NOAA Fisheries has funded restoration projects around the lake through the Great Lakes Commission, with local oversight from the West Michigan Shoreline Regional Development Commission. The work has restored and reconnected 134 acres of wetland and offshore habitat and more than 7,000 feet of shoreline. It also removed 347,350 tons of debris and 190,000 tons of contaminated soil, while improving habitat for fish and wildlife.How much habitat and shoreline was restored around Muskegon LakeThe restoration work changed several parts of the Muskegon Lake area. Since 2008, projects restored and reconnected 134 acres of wetland and offshore habitat and restored more than 7,000 feet of shoreline. They also removed 347,350 tons of debris and 190,000 tons of contaminated soil. At Veterans Memorial Park, partners restored more than 15 acres of habitat and more than 6,000 feet of shoreline. They also removed more than 40,200 metric tons of sediment. At the former Amoco site, work restored 9.8 acres of habitat and 575 feet of shoreline while removing 1,700 feet of concrete wall. Other projects restored wetlands, improved water flow and fish passage, removed dikes, and cleared logging-era sawmill debris across Muskegon.Why was Muskegon Lake removed from the Areas of Concern listMuskegon Lake was officially removed from the EPA’s Areas of Concern list in September 2025, marking the end of a process that began after its designation about 40 years earlier. The lake was listed because environmental conditions were affecting the waterway, fish and wildlife, human health, and the local economy. Partners worked for decades to address the problems required for delisting.These included fish and wildlife habitat loss, contaminated soils, and hardened shorelines. According to NOAA Fisheries, partners raised approximately $80 million for restoration in Muskegon Lake. More than $36 million came from NOAA Fisheries, primarily through the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative.Industrial pollution damaged Muskegon Lake’s water and wildlife habitatMuskegon Lake’s environmental problems developed as industries expanded around the lake in the late 1800s. Lumber mills, chemical companies, foundries, a coal-fired power plant, and a paper mill filled parts of the shoreline and contaminated the water and sediment.The contamination included compounds such as mercury and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. These conditions contributed to habitat loss and degradation, water quality concerns, and declines in fish and wildlife populations.In 1987, Muskegon Lake was listed as a Great Lakes Area of Concern. It was one of 43 ‘toxic hot spots’ in the United States and Canada. The designation was based on beneficial use impairments, which indicate how poor waterway conditions affect the environment, human health, and the local economy.Wetland restoration reconnected habitats and improved fish passageProjects also focused on reconnecting wetlands and improving habitat for fish and wildlife. At Lower Muskegon River, three dikes were removed from a former celery farm, reconnecting nearly 58 acres of wetland habitat with the river. At Bear Creek, more than 36 acres of coastal wetlands were reconnected, improving water flow and fish passage to Muskegon Lake.The project removed roughly 120,000 cubic yards of sediment containing harmful levels of phosphorus. At Muskegon Lake Nature Preserve, nearly 8 acres of wetland habitat were restored. Another project removed more than 300,600 metric tons of logging-era sawmill debris from four sites.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Elon Musk's one-word reply to David Ellison's announcement on  name of Paramount and Warner Brothers Discovery merged entity
articles.summary: David Ellison has officially announced that the newly combined entertainment powerhouse formed by Paramount and Warner Bros.
articles.body: David Ellison has officially announced that the newly combined entertainment powerhouse formed by Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will operate under the corporate banner Skydance. The announcement, made on X (formerly Twitter) marks a historic consolidation in Hollywood, bringing two century-old film and television empires under a single creative roof. Addressing the historic union, Ellison framed the new umbrella as a unified structure built to supercharge the creative output of both legacy studios. Elon Musk replied to the post with a “Congratulations” note.What David Ellison announced in his post on XAccording to Ellison, a central priority in selecting the overall corporate moniker was ensuring that neither storied brand was eclipsed or compromised by an awkward hybrid title. Ellison highlighted that both Paramount and Warner Bros. carry rich artistic pedigrees and deep global recognition that must be protected.He highlighted that both companies maintain distinct creative identities, historic production catalogs, and global franchises that have connected with generations of audiences. Rather than crafting an artificial corporate title that could diminish, alter, or overshadow either studio, leadership chose Skydance to give the holding organisation a clear corporate identity of its own.Read David Ellison's full announcementWhat once was the peak, is now just the beginning.Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling.We chose this name for a few important reasons. First and foremost, as we bring Paramount and Warner Bros. together, we wanted to preserve what has made each of these studios iconic. Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations. We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. Instead, we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks. At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance.I couldn’t be more excited about what we’re going to build together.You use AI every day. articles.title: Garbage dumping continues along Doon rivers despite crackdown
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: Garbage continues to pile up along rivers and streams across the city, with dumping rampant at several stretches despite the district
articles.body: DEHRADUN: Garbage continues to pile up along rivers and streams across the city, with dumping rampant at several stretches despite the district administration stepping up enforcement and directing civic bodies to identify illegal dumping sites and take action against offenders.A TOI spot check found plastic and household waste dumped along stretches of the Bindal and Rispana rivers and smaller streams. At Kanwali Road and Tilak Nagar, along the Bindal, residents alleged that waste from nearby shops is routinely dumped into the river.“Garbage collection vehicles come here, but many traders still dump waste into the river at night after closing their shops, either to avoid paying or because there is little fear of consequences,” said Vinay Jugral, a Tilak Nagar resident. He added that fencing along the river, similar to that at Bindal Tiraha, could help curb the practice.Similar conditions were found along the Rispana at Kandoli and towards Canal Road, where waste was scattered along the riverbanks. Large bundles of waste tied in polypropylene sacks were also found at several spots, indicating that waste collected from different locations was being brought there for dumping.The situation persists despite the district administration seeking tighter monitoring of river stretches. On Sept 5, district magistrate (DM) Ashish Chauhan directed urban local bodies to immediately identify unauthorised dumping sites, fix responsibility on agencies operating in these areas and register FIRs against people caught dumping waste into rivers. Officials were also asked to conduct regular inspections of dumping yards and strengthen surveillance at vulnerable locations.Officials were also asked by the DM to examine the feasibility of installing trash screens at drains and culverts to intercept waste before it enters rivers. A pilot project is being considered on the Rispana.DMC chief municipal health officer Anand Shukla said, “The corporation is working towards installing nets along vulnerable river stretches to restrict access and prevent dumping from both sides.”Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.body: COIMBATORE: Tamil Nadu electricity and law minister C T R Nirmal Kumar on Saturday sought an apology from DMK president M K Stalin for his “derogatory remarks” about TVK’s Dharapuram candidate P Sathyabama. articles.title: 7 of a Guwahati bar, including female staff, arrested for assault, outraging modesty of a unidentified woman
articles.summary: Guwahati: 7 staff, including female bouncers, arrested after CCTV showed assault on a woman at The Locals Bar; police also found it operating past closing time.
articles.body: Bar Found Operating Beyond Closing TimeGuwahati: Seven persons, including female bouncers, associated with a Guwahati bar have been arrested after CCTV footage purportedly showing them assaulting a woman at the bar’s basement went viral on social media on Friday.The seven persons have been arrested on charges of criminal conspiracy, assault on a woman with intent to outrage her modesty, sexual harassment, and attempt to murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.Police said that on Friday a video showing a woman being assaulted by a group of persons, including males and females, at The Locals Bar Cum Restaurant at Khanapara circulated on social media.The city police have registered a suo moto case based on an enquiry and examination of the footage since no complaint has been filed by the survivor, whose identity is still unknown.A source said that the incident started with a brawl between the survivor and a female bouncer inside the bar. The survivor allegedly hit the female bouncer after which she was dragged down to the basement.“On receipt of the information, police conducted an enquiry and examined the available CCTV footage. The footage revealed that the victim was allegedly assaulted inside the bar by a group of persons at around 2.30 AM. Thereafter, she was allegedly dragged towards the basement by pulling her hair and clothes, where she was again assaulted and appeared to become semi-conscious,” police stated.Police found that several of those involved in the assault were linked to the bar’s management and staff. Police also found the establishment was operating well past its permitted closing time of 12.30 am, and that the management had failed to inform the local police station about the incident.Those arrested include the bar manager, an event manager, a female front office executive , two female bouncers and two other males.DCP (East), of Police Commissionerate Guwahati, stated the police are examining the complete sequence of events, the role of each person involved, the bar’s operation beyond permitted hours, and any other violations that may surface during the probe.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Brazilian DJ Alok has helped restore 3 million sq m of native forest across Brazil; 400,000 seedlings have been planted
articles.summary: Brazilian DJ and music producer Alok Achkar Peres Petrillo, known simply as Alok, has taken his environmental work from the stage into forest restoration
articles.body: Brazilian DJ and music producer Alok Achkar Peres Petrillo, known simply as Alok, has taken his environmental work from the stage into forest restoration projects across Brazil. On June 1, 2026, the UN Environment Programme named Alok a Global Goodwill Ambassador, highlighting work carried out through the Alok Institute, which he founded in 2020. According to UNEP, his nature-preservation projects in the Amazon and three other Brazilian biomes have contributed to the restoration of 3 million square metres of native forest, an area equivalent to more than 300 soccer fields, with 400,000 seedlings planted. The appointment coincided with UNEP's 2026 World Environment Day campaign, which used Alok's 2022 single “Deep Down” as part of a global climate-action campaign. UNEP describes the song as a multi-platinum dance anthem that has accumulated hundreds of millions of streams worldwide.Alok's UNEP appointment brings music and environmental work togetherUNEP's announcement in Nairobi formally made Alok one of the organisation's Global Goodwill Ambassadors. The appointment followed years of philanthropic and environmental work through Instituto Alok, which UNEP says has donated nearly £8 million to social and environmental initiatives in Brazil, Africa and India. The organisation's nature projects extend beyond the Amazon to three other Brazilian biomes. UNEP says the projects have contributed to the restoration of 3 million square metres of native forest, with 400,000 seedlings planted.The 2026 World Environment Day campaign, launched on June 5, used Alok's “Deep Down” as the soundtrack for a global Climate Dance Challenge. UNEP encouraged people to participate through choreography and a question focused on limiting global warming. The campaign also included original video content from Alok, with participant videos forming part of a global music video released for World Environment Day. Alok said that nature and the knowledge and strength of Brazil's Indigenous peoples had shaped his life and music. UNEP said his work spans music, culture and social impact, including long-running projects involving Indigenous communities in the Amazon. The organisation also noted that Alok had more than 7.3 billion Spotify streams at the time of his appointment, alongside multiple awards and two Latin GRAMMY nominations.Inside Instituto Alok's Planeta Verde restoration programmeMuch of the Institute's current environmental work is organised through its Planeta Verde, or Green Planet, programme. The Institute says the programme supports reforestation, ecological restoration and biodiversity protection across different Brazilian ecosystems and biomes, while also considering the livelihoods and leadership of local communities. In Pará, the programme's Marajó Agroforestry in Family project works with the International Institute for Education of Brazil and families and organisations in the Marajó Archipelago. The Institute says 150 women involved in the project have seen their income increase by 75%, while 240,000 saplings are being planted as part of a project intended to restore about 200 hectares, or 2 million square metres. The project covers the municipalities of Breves, Curralinho, Melgaço, Muaná, Portel and São Sebastião da Boa Vista. By April 2025, the Institute reported that 76.01 hectares of agroforestry systems had already been implemented and 66,891 seedlings had been planted with the participation of 80 families.A separate Planeta Verde project is being carried out in Acre. Called Make the Forest Bloom, Field of Plenty, it involves an agroforestry restoration project covering seven hectares of land damaged by an illegal fire in 2019. The area is home to the Huwã Karu Yuxibu Centre, associated with the Huni Kuin community. In February 2025, the Alok Institute team participated in a planting event there involving nearly 2,000 seedlings, alongside SOS Amazônia volunteers, university staff and members of the Huni Kuin community. The Institute says a community nursery connected with the project is planned to produce 12,000 saplings annually. The distinction between these projects matters because the nearly 2,000 seedlings planted during the February 2025 event were part of the Acre project, not the Marajó project. The Institute's own account separately reports the planting figures for the Pará and Acre initiatives.The Future Is Ancestral puts Indigenous music at the centre of the workEnvironmental restoration is only one part of Alok's work with Indigenous communities. His project The Future Is Ancestral brought together Alok and more than 50 Indigenous musicians representing eight Brazilian Indigenous communities. According to the Alok Institute, the album involved more than 500 hours of recordings and was created to amplify Indigenous voices and preserve musical and cultural heritage. The project was developed over three years and has been presented at events including United Nations Climate Week in New York, the Global Citizen Festival and the GRAMMY Museum. The GRAMMYs reported that the album was recognised by UNESCO for its relevance to the International Decade of Indigenous Languages, while UNEP describes it as a UNESCO-recognised and GRAMMY-nominated album and philanthropic project. The project also includes work with communities such as the Yawanawá and Huni Kuin peoples. The Alok Institute says the project aims to create greater recognition of Indigenous knowledge and cultural traditions, while all revenue from the project's music is directed back towards the participating artists and communities.Rave The World turned the climate campaign into a live eventThe UNEP appointment also coincided with the launch of Rave The World, a new live performance concept developed by Alok around the principles of unity, peace, love and respect associated with rave culture. Rather than being an upcoming event, the first performance took place on June 5, 2026, at London's O2 Academy Brixton, on World Environment Day. UNEP described the concept as a way of bringing the campaign from online participation into a shared live experience.
